subject: English
summaryPoints: The past perfect tense ('had + V3') establishes chronological precedence in past narratives, designating an event completed prior to another past baseline point or simple past action.

Direct speech transforms to reported speech via tense backshifting when the reporting verb is in the past (e.g., V1 -> V2, V2 -> had + V3, has/have + V3 -> had + V3, will -> would, can -> could), alongside obligatory adjustments to person pronouns and deictic markers of time and place.

Reported questions eliminate interrogative inversion and dummy do-support: Yes/No questions introduce 'if' or 'whether' with affirmative word order, while Wh-questions retain the Wh-word followed by 'subject + verb'.

Reported orders and requests utilize reporting verbs followed by an object pronoun and an infinitive structure ('told/ordered + object + to-infinitive' or 'asked + object + to-infinitive'; negative commands use 'not to + V1').

Causative verbs 'let' and 'make' take bare infinitives in active voice (e.g., 'let him go', 'made her study'); however, when 'make' is transformed into the passive voice, it requires a full to-infinitive ('she was made to study').
Diphthongs are glided vowel phonemes where the tongue moves continuously from one vowel position to another within a single syllable (/eɪ/, /aɪ/, /ɔɪ/, /aʊ/, /əʊ/, /ɪə/, /eə/, /ʊə/).

formulas.label: Reported Question Transformation Formula
formulas.expr: Yes/No: Subject + asked + (Object) + if / whether + Subject + Verb(backshifted)  |  Wh-Question: Subject + asked + (Object) + Wh-word + Subject + Verb(backshifted)

formulas.label: Reported Command / Request Formula
formulas.expr: Affirmative: Subject + told / asked + Object + to + V1(base)  |  Negative: Subject + told / asked + Object + not to + V1(base)

formulas.label: Causative 'Let' and 'Make' Active Syntax
formulas.expr: Subject + let / make + Object (noun/pronoun) + V1(bare infinitive without 'to')

formulas.label: Causative 'Make' Passive Transformation Rule
formulas.expr: Subject + was / were made + to + V1(full to-infinitive) + (by + Agent)

examTip: A high-yield trap in EUEE reported speech is maintaining question inversion: 'He asked where did I live' is incorrect; the correct reported word order is affirmative: 'He asked where I lived.' Additionally, remember the causative shift for 'make': in the active voice, it takes a bare infinitive ('The teacher made us stay'), but in the passive voice, it strictly requires 'to' ('We were made to stay').

keyDefinitions.definition: A past verbal aspect formed with 'had' plus a past participle, expressing an action that reached completion before another specified past event.
The syntactic representation of an utterance made by another speaker, transformed without direct quotation through backshifting of tenses and deictic realignments.
A complex vowel sound in which the speech organs glide smoothly from the articulatory position of one vowel to that of another within the same syllable.
A verb (such as 'make', 'let', or 'have') that indicates that a person or entity causes an event to occur or permits someone to act.

eueeFocusTopics: Tense backshifting rules and deictic adverbial shifts in reported speech
Reported speech for Yes/No and Wh-questions (eliminating subject-auxiliary inversion)
Reported orders and requests using 'tell/ask + object + (not) to-infinitive'
Active vs passive syntax of causative 'make' (bare infinitive vs to-infinitive)
Telephone and communication phrasal verbs ('get through', 'cut off', 'hold on', 'put through')
